pairs.why: Both hounds are nearly identical; B's softer turf and gentler shading read slightly more like the smooth, clean finish of the real cards, while A's sculpted grass tufts push it toward a toy diorama.
A has the smoother ground and a cleanly shaded body that match the real cards' moderate smoothness, while B's tufted grass adds busier texture.
B's smooth turf and soft body shading are closer to the clean real-card finish than A's chunky grass tufts, but the dogs themselves are almost the same.
A has soft, even shading with a solid, well-built body that sits nearer the real cards, while B adds busier grass tufts; the difference is marginal.
B adds fine facial wrinkle detail and a dangling tag, which gives it a more texture-heavy surface, while A keeps the smoother simplified forms of the real cards.
A has finer, busier wrinkles and an extra tag, while B's simpler, smoother sculpting is closer to the real cards' moderate detail.
B's face has deeper, more numerous wrinkles and stronger saturation, while A keeps cleaner, smoother forms that match the real cards better.
A carries extra facial wrinkle texture and busier grass, while B has the simpler, smoother shading the real cards show.
